newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets tobacco target, urges restraint.
newsitem.headline: China sets tobacco target, urges restraint.

text.p: China's State Tobacco Monopoly has said tobacco leaf purchases next year should remain at the 1996 level of 230,000 tonnes, telling producers to boost quality not output, the Economic Daily said on Tuesday.
Preliminary state plans for the industry called for 1.3 million hectares of land to be planted with tobacco in 1997, the newspaper said without giving a comparison.
Producers had managed to turn around falling production of flue-cured tobacco in the first quarter of the year and had consolidated control of the industry, it quoted the state monopoly as saying.
Output should be restrained to avoid price falls that would damage both farmers and tobacco firms and Chinese growers should seek to emulate international standards of tobacco fragrance, it added.
